title: ATO's nearest-neighbour myTax prompts reached nearly 340,000 taxpayers at tax time 2020; resulting adjustments estimated by the ATO at a $37 million revenue impact
summary: ATO page: at tax time 2020 nearly 340,000 myTax users (7.5%) got real-time prompts from nearest-neighbour checks; adjustments had an estimated revenue impact of about $37 million.
account: The Australian Taxation Office's page 'How we use data and analytics' states that the ATO uses a common form of artificial intelligence known as machine learning, and that nearest neighbour methods compare amounts being entered into myTax with those of other people in similar circumstances; if a claim is significantly different from what is expected, a message prompts the taxpayer to check the figures. The page reports that during tax time in 2020 nearly 340,000 taxpayers, around 7.5% of myTax users, received a pop-up message suggesting they review a specific label, and that these prompts caused taxpayers to make adjustments estimated to have a revenue impact of around $37 million. The same page says the ATO also uses machine-learning algorithms to forecast call-centre volumes and speech recognition to transcribe inbound calls, and separately that in 2020 it automated 93,000 franking-credit refunds worth over $42 million for self-preparers over 60 (not described as machine learning). The only non-ATO source fetched is The Mandarin's report of 25 February 2025 that the Australian National Audit Office found the ATO's AI governance arrangements only partly effective; it gives no outcome figures. The earlier verifier found no non-vendor primary source with a recovered figure attributable to machine learning, and that remains the case: the $37 million is the ATO's own estimate. The page is undated; the outcome concerns tax time 2020, and the date used is 14 July 2021, the earliest Internet Archive capture of the page that already carries the 340,000 and $37 million figures (a publication-date proxy, not the event date).
purpose: Built to prompt myTax users in real time to check claims that differ from those of similar taxpayers before lodgment; the recorded adjustments are that purpose.
system: ATO myTax real-time analytics prompts using nearest-neighbour comparison models
developer: Australian Taxation Office (in-house data and analytics)
taxonomy_note: Fit: protection of public revenue and more accurate self-prepared returns. The outcome figures are the deployer's own estimates on an undated official page; the only independent source fetched (ANAO audit via The Mandarin) concerns governance, not outcomes, and its full text is paywalled.

ratings.reason: Taxpayers who corrected claims are not individually documented; the page gives no individual outcome beyond the aggregate prompt count.
The ATO's own estimate of about $37 million revenue impact from one tax time, with no independent verification and no comparison with total collections given.
Protects public revenue at modest scale: prompts reached 7.5% of myTax users and the stated impact is an estimate.

ai_role.statement: The ATO page states that nearest-neighbour methods generate the prompts and that the ATO uses machine learning; it attributes the adjustments to the prompts, while the taxpayers themselves make the changes. Only the deployer's own account was fetched for the outcome: the ATO built and runs the system in-house, so its page is both the developer's and the deployer's account (marked independent by the database's convention for public bodies describing their own tools). The ANAO audit reported by The Mandarin found AI governance 'partly effective' and offers no outcome figures in the fetched excerpt.
